dataset: 2050 real subjects, full-mask VBM; task modality excluded
microtrajectory_note: The microbenchmarks use real projected VBM samples and the production randomized-SVD initialization. After each observed batch, 1e-3 is added to the update matrix diagonal to keep every atom live; later microbatches therefore do not reproduce the exact full-fit trajectory.
hardware_note: Shared gpucw1 H100 GPU 1 had approximately 100% utilization from other jobs; short timings are observational.
precision: float64 except explicit strict-float32 comparison; TF32 disabled there

experimental_single_kernel_float64_atom_.input: Real VBM projected first 32 voxels, final dictionary; approximate codes used only to form a representative update matrix
experimental_single_kernel_float64_atom_.scope: One update microbenchmark, not a full DicL fit

interpretation: Current LARS spends most batch time in many sequential Python/PyTorch events, each solving a padded 32-by-200-by-200 system. Shrinking the solve to 64 active atoms preserved local float64 codes but yielded only about 1.1-1.3x on the four non-overflow batches. Isolated fused atom update was about 1.9x but covered a small fraction of batch time. Strict float32 did not materially improve LARS wall time. Neither candidate meets the full-stage 4.7x speed gap; no production replacement was made. A fully fused active-set LARS kernel needs separate development and full real-data validation.
